title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): G is a linear algebraic group over Q and C = Rep(G) is its Tannakian category with forgetful fibre functor omega. S is a connected complex analytic space with base point s. Grothendieck classifies tensor functors F : C -> Hodge(S), where Hodge(S) is the category of (variations of) Q-Hodge structures on S, subject to three conditions: (i) a degree/weight normalisation, with Q(-1) going to a structure of bidegree (1,1); (ii) polarisability (for each V of degree n there is phi : V⊗V -> Q(-n) such that F(phi) is a polarisation); (iii) a rigidification, i.e. an isomorphism between the fibre functor 'fibre at s of F' and omega. He calls these 'G-variations' on S.

First invariant (previous page): Pi = pi_1(S,s) acts by monodromy on the fibre functor at s. Through the rigidification this gives a homomorphism alpha : Pi -> Aut⊗(omega)(Q) = G(Q).

Second invariant (this page): pull F back to the universal cover S~. There the underlying local systems are trivialised, so each point x of S~ gives a Hodge structure on the fibre functor omega, that is, a point of the classifying space 𝒴. In modern terms 𝒴 is the space of Hodge structures on omega (homomorphisms h : S = Res_{C/R} G_m -> G_R, or the Hodge filtrations, satisfying the weight and polarisation conditions). This gives an analytic map f : S~ -> 𝒴. G(R) acts on 𝒴 on the right (the inverse of the conjugation action). The compatibility condition says f is Pi-equivariant when Pi acts on 𝒴 through alpha : Pi -> G(Q) ⊂ G(R).

Claim: rigidified G-variations (F, phi) correspond to pairs (f, alpha) satisfying these conditions. This is the period map of a variation of Hodge structure with G-structure, lifted to the universal cover, together with its monodromy representation.

Base-point-free version (bottom of the page and next page): for each s, take the fibre functor Phi_s∘F. Call F 'compatible with G' if every Phi_s∘F is isomorphic to omega, i.e. the torsor Isom⊗(omega, Phi_s∘F) is trivial over Q. Then P_s = Isom⊗(omega, Phi_s∘F) is a G(Q)-torsor. As s varies these form a principal covering P -> S with discrete group Gamma = G(Q), acting on the right. F then becomes equivalent to a pair (P, g) with g : P -> 𝒴 a Gamma-equivariant map. A deleted passage and the next page then introduce an arithmetic subgroup Gamma_0 commensurable with G(Z), fix lattices, and pass to Gamma_0-rigidified objects. This is the road to quotients Gamma_0\𝒴 as moduli of Hodge-theoretic 'motives with G-structure', i.e. Shimura-type / Mumford–Tate-domain quotients, in a Tannakian setting attached to a (motivic) Galois group G.
errors: No Griffiths transversality (horizontality) condition is imposed on f. For genuine variations of Hodge structure, f must be holomorphic and horizontal. Without it, the equivalence (F,phi) <-> (f,alpha) holds only for holomorphic families of Hodge structures, not for VHS in the later sense. This is understandable in 1965, before Griffiths's definitions became standard.

𝒴 is in general not a single G(R)-homogeneous space but a union of G(R)-orbits (G(R)-conjugacy classes of h). The page leaves it implicit that f lands in one component, which holds automatically on connected S~.

The rigidification uses the forgetful functor over Q. Fibre functors Phi_s∘F not isomorphic to omega over Q, i.e. nontrivial classes in H^1(Q,G), are excluded by fiat via the 'compatible with G' condition. These twisted forms are exactly what later matters for non-neat or twisted Shimura data. Grothendieck flags the condition but does not treat the twisted case.
Equivariance conventions (left versus right action, alpha versus alpha^{-1}) are only sketched; the marginal correction 'à droite ... (opposée à l'action gauche)' shows he was fixing them on the fly.

ideas.what: Hodge structures (and families of them) with G-structure, defined as tensor functors Rep(G) -> Hodge(S) with polarisation and weight conditions
ideas.modern_name: Variation of Hodge structure with G-structure / Tannakian description of Mumford–Tate data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Travaux de Shimura 1971; Variétés de Shimura 1979; Hodge II–III); Saavedra Rivano (1972) for the Tannakian formalism; Mumford (1966) for Hodge groups
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted via Saavedra's thesis and Deligne; not in any Grothendieck publication to my knowledge

ideas.what: Equivalence between rigidified G-variations and pairs (period map f : S~ -> 𝒴, monodromy alpha : pi_1 -> G(Q)) with f equivariant
ideas.modern_name: Period map / monodromy description of VHS; Mumford–Tate domains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (1968–70) for period domains and period maps; Green–Griffiths–Kerr (2012) for Mumford–Tate domains

ideas.what: Base-point-free formulation: principal G(Q)-covering P = Isom⊗(omega, fibre functors) with a Gamma-equivariant map P -> 𝒴, then quotient by an arithmetic subgroup Gamma_0 commensurable with G(Z)
ideas.modern_name: Shimura-variety / arithmetic quotient Gamma\D as moduli of Hodge structures with G-structure

ideas.what: Condition that the fibre functors Phi_s∘F are isomorphic to omega (triviality of a G-torsor over Q)
ideas.modern_name: Neutral fibre functor / triviality of the class in H^1(Q,G)
ideas.where_published: Saavedra Rivano, Catégories tannakiennes (1972), written under Grothendieck's direction

missed.claim: In 1965, before Mumford's 1966 Hodge-group paper and Griffiths's period-domain papers, Grothendieck formulated variations of Hodge structure with G-structure Tannakianly. He classified them by (equivariant period map to the space 𝒴 of Hodge structures on the fibre functor of Rep G, monodromy into G(Q)), and gave a base-point-free version as a principal G(Q)-covering with equivariant map to 𝒴. This is essentially the Tannakian framework later used by Deligne for Shimura varieties.
missed.quote: La donnée d'un couple (F, φ) équivaut à celle d'un couple (f, α) satisfaisant les deux conditions précédentes.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that the Tannakian approach to period domains and Shimura-type moduli originated with Grothendieck in the motivic Galois group programme of 1965. It is relevant to the history and credit of Deligne's 1971/1979 formalism and of Mumford–Tate domains.

missed.claim: The passage to arithmetic level structures (lattices and a discrete subgroup commensurable with G(Z)) is started and struck out here, then resumed on the next page. The links to transversality and to the algebraicity of Gamma_0\𝒴 are not addressed.
missed.quote: Il faudrait fixer des réseaux, et des sous-groupes discrets commensurables de G(Q), du type G(Z)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mostly superseded by the theory of Shimura varieties and Mumford–Tate domains (where Gamma\D is generally non-algebraic). Its interest is as a record of motivation rather than as new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is now standard: period maps, G-structures, and Shimura data as quotients Gamma\X. Its appearance in Grothendieck's 1965 motivic Galois notes, phrased Tannakianly with G(Q)-coverings and arithmetic subgroups, predates Mumford (1966), Griffiths and Deligne. It is not documented in the published record, making it a notable but not revolutionary historical detail.
transcription_corrections: The symbol transcribed as 𝔥 is a script letter, likely the same 𝒴 used on the next page for the classifying space of Hodge structures.
'Φ_s (mot/Q)' is an interlinear insertion naming the fibre functor at s (on the next page written ℒ_s or Φ_s); 'mot/Q' plausibly indicates motives over Q.
The bracketed 'Données ... le G-...' line is likely a correction introducing 'G-subordination' (or a similar coinage), matching the next page's 'G-subordinations'.
'compatible avec les actions de Π' and the insertion '{+à droite+}' over 'l'action de G(R)' are correctly placed; the parenthetical reads '(opposée à l'action gauche)'.
